problem: The chapter says the same region can be described as type I and type II, but never warns that some regions fail the new description and must be split into two integrals before the order can be changed. A student meeting such a sketch will force a single pair of limits and get a wrong answer.
fix: Add one line after the four steps: if a horizontal line through R enters or leaves through different curves on different parts of the y-range, split R into pieces with a horizontal cut, change order on each piece, and add the results.

problem: The line 'I = ∫₀¹ [x e^(y²)] from x=0 to x=y dy' puts the dy inside the bracket, so it reads as if dy is part of the evaluated expression rather than the outer differential.
fix: Write it as I = ∫₀¹ (∫₀ʸ e^(y²) dx) dy = ∫₀¹ [x e^(y²)]<sub>x=0</sub><sup>x=y</sup> dy = ∫₀¹ y e^(y²) dy.
